headline: 3-0 win: Spain sweep aside Austria to reach World Cup last 16
summary: Mikel Oyarzabal's double leads La Roja to a dominant victory, maintaining their shutout streak in the tournament.
details: Spain secured a place in the World Cup round of 16 after a dominant 3-0 victory over Austria on Thursday. Mikel Oyarzabal powered the win with two goals, while the team maintained its perfect defensive record by not conceding a single goal so far in the tournament.

The breakthrough came when Marc Cucurella delivered a precise cross that Oyarzabal steered into the bottom corner. Despite strong saves from Austrian goalkeeper Alexander Schlager, Spain remained the aggressors throughout the first half.

Pedro Porro added a second goal in the 66th minute with a header, playing in front of a sold-out crowd that included celebrities Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem. Oyarzabal then capped off the performance with his fourth goal of the tournament in the 89th minute.
Spain's path to the quarter-finals now leads them to a match against either Portugal or Croatia. The team showed significant improvement from their opening goalless draw against Cape Verde.
The victory also highlighted the return to form of 18-year-old Lamine Yamal, who appeared to have recovered from a hamstring injury that had limited his impact earlier in the competition.
caption:
Spain is through! 🇪🇸

A dominant 3-0 win over Austria sends La Roja into the World Cup round of 16.

Spain secured a place in the World Cup round of 16 after a dominant 3-0 victory over Austria on Thursday. Mikel Oyarzabal powered the win with two goals, while the team maintained its perfect defensive record by not conceding a single goal so far in the tournament.

The breakthrough came when Marc Cucurella delivered a precise cross that Oyarzabal steered into the bottom corner. Despite strong saves from Austrian goalkeeper Alexander Schlager, Spain remained the aggressors throughout the first half.

Pedro Porro added a second goal in the 66th minute with a header, playing in front of a sold-out crowd that included celebrities Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem. Oyarzabal then capped off the performance with his fourth goal of the tournament in the 89th minute.

Spain's path to the quarter-finals now leads them to a match against either Portugal or Croatia. The team showed significant improvement from their opening goalless draw against Cape Verde.

The victory also highlighted the return to form of 18-year-old Lamine Yamal, who appeared to have recovered from a hamstring injury that had limited his impact earlier in the competition.

headline: Israel's parliament advances bill to restrict mosque loudspeakers
summary: The Knesset voted 50-36 in a preliminary reading to tighten controls on the call to prayer, sparking accusations of targeting the Muslim minority.
details: Israel's parliament, the Knesset, has passed a bill in its preliminary reading with a 50-36 vote. The proposal would tighten restrictions on the use of loudspeakers in mosques for the call to prayer.
The bill, introduced by far-right lawmaker Zvika Fogel, would require mosques to obtain official permits to operate their loudspeaker systems.
Under the new rules, police would be authorized to enter mosque premises to stop violations and impose administrative fines on those who fail to comply.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir supported the move, claiming that governance begins with noise control and that residents of Arab communities are also affected by the broadcasts.
Arab lawmakers have strongly rejected these claims, accusing the government of unfairly singling out the Muslim minority and attempting to silence the community.
The vote was made possible after the ultra-Orthodox Shas party shifted its position and decided to back the bill, despite previous understandings with Arab lawmakers.
Efforts to limit mosque loudspeakers have been a long-standing goal for right-wing politicians and activists, following complaints from Jewish residents about excessive noise.
Arabs, who make up approximately 20 percent of the isreali population, mostly Muslims, view the call to prayer as a fundamental part of their daily religious life.
